acceptance: 1) Entry: visitor contact-window Send -> received; operator admin Human conversations -> actual row -> Send reply (operator-chat-send). Data sources: POST /api/admin/chat/conversations/[id]/messages and both parties' GETs. Clicking send actually saves author/body; visitor polling displays the same human message, with no AI-generated reply. Database persistence failure produces no received state (E-16, E-31). 2) Two real operators replying concurrently retain both seq/author values. Clicking Close conversation (operator-chat-close) sends PATCH expectedVersion. On conflict read current state without automatic overwrite; closed sends from either party get 409. The next send after revocation gets 403 and creates no row. Notification failure changes only notification state (E-32, E-33, E-35, E-41, E-78). Use the unique minimalist-flat style from section 11. At the actual service at 1920x1080, 1440x900, and 390x844, record GIFs and computed styles: 2px black borders, zero radius, no shadow, and accent #b45700. On each admin page, run D1-D6 and overflow probes with work/form/card and density7/gutter16/gap16/pad16. Labels and keyboard focus are reachable; touch-control targets measure at least 44px.

E-16.trigger: A visitor sends the first message while an operator is online.
E-16.expect: Persist the conversation and message before showing a received state. The operator inbox can read it and send a human reply; do not generate an automated AI answer.

E-31.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-31.trigger: A visitor submits a message and server-side persistence succeeds.
E-31.expect: Return stable conversation and message identifiers and show Received, with the conversation readable in the operator inbox. If the database write fails, retain a retry-pending state and do not show Received or read by an operator.

E-32.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-32.trigger: The requester is unauthenticated, an EDITOR, an account whose privileges were revoked, or a visitor guessing someone else's conversation identifier.
E-32.expect: Directly request the read and reply endpoints for each of these cases and verify no content is returned and no write occurs. Return data to ADMIN/SALES only under current authorization; hiding a button is not authorization evidence.

E-33.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-33.trigger: Two authorized people reply concurrently, or a visitor repeats the same client message identifier.
E-33.expect: Order by server seq and show the actual author. The same clientMessageId and payload in the same conversation produce only one message, one outbox item, and one unread increment. Persist each concurrent human reply; a later response must not overwrite an earlier saved reply.

E-35.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-35.trigger: An email notification fails or is not connected.
E-35.expect: Represent the actual notification state using the defined queued/sending/sent/failed states or their existing DTO mapping. Notification failure after a message is saved changes only that notification state, not the message's received state or the inbox's ability to process it. An unconnected source must not display Sent.

E-41.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-41.trigger: A message has been saved but an operator reply or notification fails to send.
E-41.expect: Keep the received result and inbox pending-work state. Separately show the real sending failure; do not pretend that the visitor has been contacted.

E-78.trigger: A visitor session expires or is revoked, or an operator loses chat permission after previously holding ADMIN/SALES.
E-78.expect: Perform server-side authorization on the next poll and send, and stop returning conversation content. Changing threadId, seq, or email cannot read another consultation.
